notes: ArrayList is finished. Topic 4.10 is the six standard algorithms on a list: totalling and averaging, the largest and smallest, counting and the any and all flags, finding a value, building a second list, and comparing each element with the next. Six concepts, seventeen exercises, and it is deliberately the same six as the 2D array topic, because they are the same six and nobody should have to learn them twice.

Every trap in it is a real one with a real reason. Starting a maximum at 0 and getting an answer that is not in the list. An average that prints 5.0 when it should print 5.666, because both sides of the slash were ints and the decimals were gone before the double got a look in. A counter declared inside the loop. An any check with an else that throws its own answer away. A search with nothing stopping it, so it reports the last match instead of the first.
The course now teaches 39 of the College Board's 57 topics, and all three ArrayList topics are among them, which is the whole of free response question 3.
